titleTh: ขอเงินมัดจำห้องเช่าคืน
scenarioSentences: You recently moved out of an apartment.
Your landlord, Mr. Walsh, kept half your deposit.
He says you stained the carpet.
You believe the stain was there before.
You call him to sort it out.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Mr. Walsh. I'm calling because half my deposit is missing.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Walsh
dialogue.text: I kept it to clean the stain on the carpet.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: But that stain was already there when I moved in.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Walsh
dialogue.text: Can you prove that? I don't remember it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I took photos on my first day, and the stain is clearly visible.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Walsh
dialogue.text: I see. Could you email them to me today?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Sure. If they show the stain, will you return the full amount?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Walsh
dialogue.text: If it's the same stain, yes. But the kitchen shelf is broken too.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fair. I did break it, so take the repair cost from the deposit.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Walsh
dialogue.text: All right. I'll check the photos and send you the rest by Friday.

titleTh: ต่อรองค่าเช่าที่จะขึ้น
scenarioSentences: Your lease ends soon.
Your landlord, Ms. Duarte, wants to raise the rent.
She is asking for fifteen percent more.
You like the apartment, but that is too much.
You go to see her.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Ms. Duarte, fifteen percent is a big jump. I'm not sure I can manage it.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Duarte
dialogue.text: I understand, but my repair costs and taxes have gone up this year.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I've always paid on time. Would you accept a smaller rise?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Duarte
dialogue.text: What did you have in mind?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Five percent. Otherwise, I'll have to look for somewhere cheaper.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Duarte
dialogue.text: Five is too low. But if you signed for two years, I could accept eight.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Eight percent is reasonable, as long as it stays fixed for both years.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Duarte
dialogue.text: Agreed. I'll put that in the new contract and email it by Friday.

titleEn: Agreeing on cleaning rules with a roommate
titleTh: ตกลงกติกาทำความสะอาดกับรูมเมท
scenarioSentences: You share an apartment with Alex.
The kitchen is always messy.
Dirty dishes stay in the sink for days.
You are tired of cleaning up after him.
You bring it up tonight.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Alex, can we talk about the kitchen? Those dishes have been in the sink since Monday.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Sorry, I've been working late. I was going to wash them this weekend.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I understand, but I always end up cleaning everything. It isn't fair.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: You're right. Should we make a weekly cleaning schedule?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes. We could take turns with the kitchen each week.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Honestly, I'd rather clean the bathroom every week than do the kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: In that case, the bathroom is yours, and I'll do the kitchen. But wash your own dishes the same day.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: That's reasonable. I'll start with the bathroom on Saturday.

titleEn: Asking a manager to cut work hours
titleTh: ขอลดกะทำงานช่วงสอบ
scenarioSentences: You work part-time at a bookstore.
Your manager is Mr. Fowler.
Your final exams start in three weeks.
You need more time to study.
You ask him for a quick chat.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Fowler, my final exams start soon. Could I work fewer shifts for a while?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fowler
dialogue.text: How many fewer? We're already short of staff this month.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'm working four shifts a week now. Two would really help.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fowler
dialogue.text: Two is difficult. Could you manage three if one was on Sunday?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Sundays are fine, as long as they're short. I'd rather study in the mornings.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fowler
dialogue.text: Okay. Three shifts, including a short Sunday afternoon. How long do you need?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Just one month. My last exam is at the end of May.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fowler
dialogue.text: In that case, you'll go back to four shifts in June. Is that fair?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, thank you. That's a reasonable compromise.

titleTh: เปลี่ยนเที่ยวบินหลังตกเครื่องต่อ
scenarioSentences: Your first flight landed an hour late.
You missed your connecting flight home.
You are stuck at the airport.
Ms. Varga works at the airline desk.
You ask her for help.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi. My first flight was an hour late, so I missed my connection.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Varga
dialogue.text: I'm sorry. The next flight with free seats leaves at nine tonight.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's a seven-hour wait. Is there anything earlier?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Varga
dialogue.text: There's one at four, but it stops twice and arrives later.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then I'd rather take the direct one. Do I get anything for the long wait?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Varga
dialogue.text: Since the delay was our fault, I can give you a meal voucher for the airport restaurants.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. Could you also make sure my bag goes on the new flight?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Varga
dialogue.text: Yes, it'll go on the new flight. Here's your boarding pass for gate twelve.

titleTh: เคลมพัสดุที่แตกเสียหาย
scenarioSentences: You sent a glass vase to your aunt.
It arrived in pieces.
You paid extra for careful handling.
Mr. Bell works at the post office.
You go to see him.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello. I sent a vase last week with careful handling, and it arrived broken.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Bell
dialogue.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Was it packed in a strong box with padding?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, I wrapped it carefully. My aunt took photos of the box and the pieces.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Bell
dialogue.text: Good, that's useful evidence. You'll need to fill in a claim form.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Fine. Will I get the full value back, or only the delivery cost?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Bell
dialogue.text: Both, as long as you have the receipt for the vase.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I do. How long does it usually take?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Bell
dialogue.text: About two weeks. Please attach the photos, and I'll send the claim today.

titleEn: Sharing the cost of a fence repair
titleTh: หารค่าซ่อมรั้วกับเพื่อนบ้าน
scenarioSentences: A storm broke the fence behind your house.
You share the fence with your neighbor, Mr. Dalton.
It needs to be fixed quickly.
Nobody has discussed the cost yet.
You knock on his door.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, Mr. Dalton. Did you see the fence? The storm broke three sections.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Dalton
dialogue.text: I did. It's a mess. My dog could get out, so it needs fixing soon.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I agree. Since it's a shared fence, should we split the cost?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Dalton
dialogue.text: That seems fair. Do you know a builder? I don't want someone too expensive.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not really. I'm busy all week, so could you find someone?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Dalton
dialogue.text: Fine. I'll get two quotes and pick the cheaper one, if that's okay.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That works, as long as it's under four hundred dollars in total.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Dalton
dialogue.text: Reasonable. I'll call some builders tomorrow and let you know the price.

titleEn: Planning a trip with different budgets
titleTh: วางแผนเที่ยวทั้งที่งบไม่เท่ากัน
scenarioSentences: You and your friend Nina are planning a beach trip.
You will be away for four nights.
Nina wants to stay in hotels.
You can only afford hostels.
You talk it over at lunch.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Nina, I've checked prices. Four nights in a hotel would use up my whole budget.

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: But hostels are so noisy. I'd rather pay more and actually sleep.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I understand. What if we stayed in a hostel with private rooms?

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: That could work, but I'd still like one special night somewhere nice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Fair enough. Three nights in a hostel, then a hotel on the last night?

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: Perfect. And since the hotel was my idea, I'll pay a bigger share.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's really kind. Then I'll book the hostel tonight, and you choose the hotel.

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: Deal. I'll send you a few options tomorrow.

titleTh: โต้แย้งใบสั่งจอดรถ
scenarioSentences: You got a parking fine on campus yesterday.
The area was a no-parking zone.
However, a tree was covering the sign.
Officer Ruiz works at the parking office.
You go there to explain.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Officer Ruiz. I got a fine yesterday, but I don't think it's fair.

dialogue.speaker: Officer Ruiz
dialogue.text: Where were you parked? The fine says it was a no-parking zone.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Behind the library. The sign is completely hidden by a tree, so I couldn't see it.

dialogue.speaker: Officer Ruiz
dialogue.text: Drivers are responsible for checking. Do you have any evidence?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, I took these photos this morning. You can't see the sign from the road.

dialogue.speaker: Officer Ruiz
dialogue.text: Let me look. You're right, the branches cover it completely.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: So will you cancel the fine?

dialogue.speaker: Officer Ruiz
dialogue.text: Yes, I'll cancel it today. I'll also ask the gardeners to cut that tree back.

titleEn: Deciding whether to take a gap year
titleTh: ตัดสินใจเรื่องพักเรียนหนึ่งปี
scenarioSentences: You have a university place for September.
You also want to work and travel first.
Your parents think it is a bad idea.
Ms. Kowalski is your careers advisor.
You ask for her advice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Ms. Kowalski, I'm thinking about a gap year, but I don't want to lose my university place.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kowalski
dialogue.text: Many universities will hold your place for a year. Have you asked yours?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not yet. My parents are worried I'll never go back.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kowalski
dialogue.text: That happens if the year has no plan. What would you actually do?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Work for six months to save money, then travel and maybe volunteer.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kowalski
dialogue.text: That's a reasonable plan, as long as you set a budget and dates.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: So should I ask the university to hold my place until next year?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kowalski
dialogue.text: Yes, before the deadline in March. Then show your parents a written plan.

titleEn: Fixing an error in the club budget
titleTh: แก้ตัวเลขผิดในงบชมรม
scenarioSentences: You look after the money for the photography club.
Leah is the club president.
The budget report goes to members on Friday.
You just found a mistake in it.
You call Leah right away.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Leah, I found a mistake in the budget. The bus for the trip was counted twice.

dialogue.speaker: Leah
dialogue.text: Oh no. How much difference does that make?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Three hundred dollars. We actually have more money left than the report says.

dialogue.speaker: Leah
dialogue.text: Well, that's better than less. But members will notice if the numbers change later.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I know. I'd rather fix it now than explain it at the meeting.

dialogue.speaker: Leah
dialogue.text: Agreed. Can you send me a corrected version by Thursday evening?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Sure. Should I mention the change in the email to members?

dialogue.speaker: Leah
dialogue.text: Yes, just a short note. Otherwise, people might think we're hiding something.

titleEn: Asking a coach for more playing time
titleTh: ขอโค้ชให้ได้ลงเล่นมากขึ้น
scenarioSentences: You play on the college basketball team.
Coach Bennett is in charge of the team.
You never miss training.
But you sit on the bench in most games.
You ask to speak with him.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Coach, can I ask you something? I train hard, but I hardly play in games.

dialogue.speaker: Coach Bennett
dialogue.text: I've noticed how hard you work. Your shooting has really improved.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks. So what's stopping you from putting me in?

dialogue.speaker: Coach Bennett
dialogue.text: Your defense. You lose your player too easily, and that costs us points.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fair. What can I do to fix it?

dialogue.speaker: Coach Bennett
dialogue.text: Stay after training on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We'll work on defense together.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'll be there. If I get better, will I play more?

dialogue.speaker: Coach Bennett
dialogue.text: If I see real progress, you'll start getting ten minutes a game next month.

titleEn: Asking a friend to repay a loan
titleTh: ทวงเงินที่เพื่อนยืม
scenarioSentences: Your friend Marco borrowed money two months ago.
He promised to pay it back soon.
He has not mentioned it since.
Now you need the money for rent.
You bring it up over coffee.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Marco, this is a bit awkward, but do you remember the three hundred dollars?

dialogue.speaker: Marco
dialogue.text: Of course. I'm sorry, I meant to pay you back weeks ago.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's okay, but my rent is due on the first, and I'm short.

dialogue.speaker: Marco
dialogue.text: I understand. The problem is that I can't pay it all right now.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: How much could you manage this month?

dialogue.speaker: Marco
dialogue.text: I could give you one fifty on Friday, and the rest at the end of the month.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That works, as long as the second part really comes on time.

dialogue.speaker: Marco
dialogue.text: It will, I promise. I'll send it the day I get paid.

titleEn: Getting permission for a charity run
titleTh: ขออนุญาตจัดงานวิ่งการกุศล
scenarioSentences: Your student group is organizing a charity run.
The route goes through the old town.
The city must approve it.
Mr. Haddad works at the city events office.
You meet him to discuss it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Haddad, we'd like to hold a charity run on the last Sunday of April.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Haddad
dialogue.text: Let me see your route. This part goes through the market street.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes. Is that a problem?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Haddad
dialogue.text: The market is open on Sundays, so it isn't safe for runners.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We could go along the river instead. It's a bit longer, though.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Haddad
dialogue.text: That's much better. How many volunteers will you have at the crossings?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: About twenty. Would that be enough?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Haddad
dialogue.text: Yes, as long as each one wears a safety vest. Submit the application by April first.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll send it with the new route map next week.

titleTh: แจ้งธนาคารเรื่องข้อความน่าสงสัย
scenarioSentences: You got a strange text this morning.
It looked like it came from your bank.
It asked you to click a link.
You did not click it.
You call Ms. Price at your bank.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Ms. Price. I got a text saying my account was locked, with a link.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Price
dialogue.text: We never send links by text. Did you click on it?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: No, it looked suspicious, so I called you instead.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Price
dialogue.text: Good decision. Did you reply or share any card details?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: No. But they knew my name, which worries me.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Price
dialogue.text: That's common with fake messages. To be safe, I'd suggest blocking your card.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'd rather not. I need it this week.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Price
dialogue.text: I understand, but it's safer. A new card will arrive in three days.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: All right, block it. Can I still take out cash at the branch?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Price
dialogue.text: Yes, with your ID. I'm blocking it now.
